title: A cue repeated
hook: A repeated event can be met with a changing response.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In this toy record, responses to the same harmless cue are 4, 3, 2, then 1. What happens across those four trials?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In this toy record, responses to the same harmless cue are 4, 3, 2, then 1. What happens across those four trials?

claims.text: In this toy record, responses to the same harmless cue are 4, 3, 2, then 1. What happens across those four trials? The two panels show response levels 4, 3, 2 and 1 across the stipulated trials. The response decreases in this example, a pattern consistent with habituation. The record alone does not rule out fatigue, sensory changes or other explanations.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A response has levels 5, 4, 3, 2 after four repeated cues. What is the visible trend? The listed values decrease from one trial to the next.
